plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win but the second-highest bid exceeds my value; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $42, I should bid exactly $42 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever the price paid (second-highest bid) is below my true value, capturing all available surplus.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. If I bid my true value of $29, I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay only that second-highest bid - ensuring I never overpay and always capture positive surplus when I win. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' behavior. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing a profitable auction. With a value of $48, I will bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.
